followup_reviews.Research finding: Actual bilateral goods stoppage and restoration remain supported; the January 17–19 ANI episode is a separate lead and is excluded from this parent. Keep goods exchange in both directions, with internal loading/unloading continuing. Neither official claims about fraudulent licences nor industry allegations establish a universal passenger restriction. Retain 31 January–5 February 2022 and five calendar days. Direct contemporary onset and two authorities’ actual-restoration accounts outweigh later February 1 wording, which stays explicit. Thursday strike withdrawal and Friday holiday prevent treating the interval as five active strike days. Keep Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests for the port users’ stated document/entry grievances. State inspection rationale and alleged smuggling are contextual, not replacement official rationales for the port-user stoppage. Fresh reopening, TOI and Awaaz bodies supplement the cached contemporary onset. TOI quotes a different named official; its two articles share a publisher. Awaaz’s unverified original chain and same-text mirror are not independent origins. The phase remains unlocated with no invented point or border outline. Additional sources are attached to evidence only, preserving temporal and geographic limits.
